fixes.title: RESIDUAL: rise and set are reported a whole day late for every target that culminates in the afternoon
fixes.summary: Wave 4 saw this while probing finding 1, called it 'worth a finding of its own' and deliberately left it. It is the same defect class and much larger than the 4-minute slip. calculateObjectVisibility scans local noon to local noon; when the object is already up as that window opens, the first crossing found is a SET and the next RISE belongs to the following day. The solver kept that late rise and then hunted FORWARD for a set to match it, so both ends landed ~24 h after the events they described while the transit stayed on the right day — rise after transit, set 30 h after it. Denver, night of 2024-01-15, RA 22h Dec +20 came back rise 2024-01-16 07:03 / transit 2024-01-15 14:20 / set 2024-01-16 21:30 for a target that actually rose 07:07 and set 21:33 on the 15th. That is the whole early-evening half of the sky. Fixed by letting the TRANSIT — the window's altitude maximum, so the culmination the window was opened for — decide which pass is reported: when the peak precedes the late rise, keep the in-window set and walk BACKWARDS from the window start for the rise that began the pass (new _findRiseBefore); otherwise keep the existing forward-set repair, which is right for a pass that starts late in the window. Three consumers had already grown workarounds for this — sequence_emitter.dart shifts crossings by whole sidereal days, TargetWindow.isVisibleAt short-circuits to a live altitude solve ('a target at the zenith came back as rises at 03:41 tomorrow'), and target_scoring stopped gating its rises-late warning on riseTime — all of which keep working, now on correct inputs.
fixes.revert_check: Deleted the transit-anchored branch and put the repair back to the single `if (riseTime != null && setTime != null && !setTime.isAfter(riseTime))` forward-set search. 'a block that outlasts the target raises the conflict' FAILED with 'conflicts were []' — six hours of subs on a target that sets three hours in passed pre-flight in total silence, because the mid-block conflict is gated on `end.isAfter(setTime)` and no node ending tonight is after a set reported for tomorrow. 'the window names the set on the night the run is in' FAILED too, as did both bracketing tests ('rise 2024-01-16 09:03 is not before transit 2024-01-15 16:20'). Restored: 4/4 pass, planetarium 477/477, estimator+smart-night 51/51.
fixes.caveats: TWO EXISTING TESTS WERE EDITED and both edits need a reviewer's eye. (1) sunrise_sunset_refraction_test.dart asserted calculateSunVisibility().riseTime equalled the NEXT morning's sunrise while its own transit was the previous afternoon — an incoherent triple. It now asserts the sunSET against the same NOAA ground truth (matches expectedSunsetUtc to under a second), the rise<transit<set invariant, and that the rise is one solar day before the old expectation. calculateSunVisibility's doc now points callers wanting the dusk->dawn span at calculateTwilightTimes, which is what the dashboard night strip actually uses; the only production caller reads .neverRises. (2) target_scoring_rises_late_test.dart opened by SEARCHING for a sky whose solved rise fell after the night ended — the defect premise — and that sky no longer exists, so the search returned null. The premise is now an assertion that it cannot exist ('a target 60+ deg up at dusk rose before dusk, not after dawn'); the test's actual guard, that the scorer raises no notYetRisen warning, is unchanged and still passes.
